packet.headline_seed: World leaders congratulate Andy Burnham as he becomes Britain’s PM
packet.description_seed: Beyond the diplomatic platitudes global media focuses on the ‘immense’ scale of the challenge he faces in the job UK politics live – latest updates World leaders have warmly congratulated Andy Burnham on his entry into 10 Downing Street as Britain’s seventh prime minister in a decade, but international media largely focused on the scale of the challenges awaiting him. Emmanuel Macron, France’s president, said he hoped for a deeper relationship “in the service of our peoples, and by giving new momentum to the partnership between the UK and the EU” rekindled by Burnham’s predecessor, Keir Starmer. Beyond the diplomatic platitudes global media focuses on the ‘immense’ scale of the challenge he faces in the job World leaders have warmly congratulated Andy Burnham on his entry into 10 Downing Street as Britain’s seventh prime minister in a decade, but international media largely focused on the scale of the challenges awaiting him. Emmanuel Macron, France’s president, said he hoped for a deeper relationship “in the service of our peoples, and by giving new momentum to the partnership between the UK and the EU” rekindled by Burnham’s predecessor, Keir Starmer. The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, who spoke with Burnham on Monday evening including about continued support for Ukraine, said Germany and the UK were close partners and he looked forward to working together.

President hopes UK, under Burnham will contribute towards ending hostilities in ME and restoring Islamabad MoU President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday congratulated newly appointed United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham on assuming office and expressed their desire to strengthen cooperation with the incoming leader. Burnham became Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade, pledging to break with the politics of the past to deliver a new economic model to benefit a nation "fed up" with a revolving door of leaders. King Charles III appointed Burnham as prime minister after outgoing leader Keir Starmer formally tendered his resignation, Buckingham Palace said. According to a statement issued by the President's Office, Zardari hoped that under Burnham’s leadership, Pakistan and the UK would further strengthen their longstanding bilateral partnership and expand cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

The president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, said she looked forward to “strengthening the EU-UK partnership”. A “very good first discussion” had revealed a common commitment to “bringing the EU and UK closer and closer”, she later added. Beyond the diplomatic platitudes, however, media coverage focused on Burnham’s regional persona – and the huge task awaiting him. France’s Public Sénat said the new prime minister came from “the working class of the north of England”. He had managed to “build an image as an ‘everyman’, appearing without a tie, very often in a T-shirt”, the political TV channel said on its website, standing out as “a politician on the ground, close to everyday concerns”.

Emmanuel Macron, France’s president, said he hoped for a deeper relationship “in the service of our peoples, and by giving new momentum to the partnership between the UK and the EU” rekindled by Burnham’s predecessor, Keir Starmer.

The president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, said she looked forward to “strengthening the EU-UK partnership”. A “very good first discussion” had revealed a common commitment to “bringing the EU and UK closer and closer”, she later added.

Beyond the diplomatic platitudes, however, media coverage focused on Burnham’s regional persona – and the huge task awaiting him. France’s Public Sénat said the new prime minister came from “the working class of the north of England”.

He had managed to “build an image as an ‘everyman’, appearing without a tie, very often in a T-shirt”, the political TV channel said on its website, standing out as “a politician on the ground, close to everyday concerns”.

Italy’s Corriere della Sera said the UK was experiencing “profound unease, instability and social resentment” and “needs a push” forward, but Burnham’s nationalisation, state intervention and reindustrialisation plans suggested he saw the past as a model.

Andy Burnham sworn in as U.K. prime minister

Andy Burnham became the fifth British prime minister in four years and the seventh in a decade as he formally accepted an invitation Monday from King Charles to form a government.

The meeting quickly followed on the heels of Keir Starmer offering his resignation.

Burnham secured nominations from 379 of the 403 Labour lawmakers in the House of Commons to officially became leader of the Labour Party last week.

Britain's parliamentary democracy allows governing parties to change leaders, and thus prime ministers, without the need for a general election. The next national election doesn't have to be held until 2029.

In his first speech as prime minister, Burnham said he hoped to be a "circuit breaker" to end the trend of instability in British politics.

"Britain ⁠needs to show the world that we ‌can regain our stability once again," Burnham said outside ⁠10 Downing Street.

"We have ⁠not been good ⁠enough, ⁠and ​we need to be ​better."

In ​a clip recorded before he was officially appointed as British ​leader but released after his ⁠speech in ⁠Downing Street, Burnham ‌said that among his first telephone calls internationally would be U.S. President Donald Trump and Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

"President Zelenskyy will be ⁠left ⁠in ​no doubt whatsoever that Britain's support is steadfast, ​it is ⁠resolute. It will be there for him, and I will be there for him personally, too," Burnham told reporters.

Can the 'King of the North' fix a fractured Britain?

Carney congratulates new U.K. Prime Minister Burnham, calls for continued co-operation

Zelenskyy was among a number of world leaders to offer congratulations to Burnham on social media, a list that included Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.

"I look forward to working with Prime Minister Burnham to build greater security, stability and prosperity on both sides of the Atlantic," said Carney.

The White House confirmed Monday that Burnham and Trump spoke briefly. Burnham's predecessor ingratiated himself with Trump for more than a year, only for the U.S. president to later express frustration over what he perceived as Starmer's lack of support for the Iran war.

payload.title: Kansainväliset johtajat onnittelivat Britannian uutta pääministeriä Andy Burnhamia
payload.summary: Andy Burnham on nimitetty Britannian pääministeriksi Keir Starmerin eron jälkeen. Onnittelujen rinnalla kansainvälinen huomio kohdistuu Britannian suuriin poliittisiin ja taloudellisiin haasteisiin.
payload.content:
Andy Burnham on noussut Britannian pääministeriksi Keir Starmerin jätettyä eronpyyntönsä. Kuningas Charles III nimitti Burnhamin tehtävään, ja hänestä tuli maan seitsemäs pääministeri kymmenen vuoden aikana. Kansainväliset johtajat onnittelivat Burnhamia mutta korostivat samalla yhteistyön jatkamista Britannian kanssa.

## Euroopassa toivotaan tiiviimpiä suhteita

Ranskan presidentti Emmanuel Macron ilmaisi toiveensa Britannian ja Ranskan suhteiden syventämisestä. Hän haluaa myös antaa uutta vauhtia Britannian ja Euroopan unionin kumppanuudelle, jota Burnhamin edeltäjä Starmer oli ryhtynyt elvyttämään.

Euroopan komission puheenjohtaja Ursula von der Leyen kertoi odottavansa EU:n ja Britannian kumppanuuden vahvistamista. Hän kuvaili ensimmäistä keskusteluaan Burnhamin kanssa erittäin hyväksi ja sanoi osapuolten jakavan tavoitteen EU:n ja Britannian lähentämisestä.

Saksan liittokansleri Friedrich Merz keskusteli Burnhamin kanssa maanantai-iltana. Keskustelussa käsiteltiin muun muassa Ukrainan tukemisen jatkamista. Merz luonnehti Saksaa ja Britanniaa läheisiksi kumppaneiksi ja ilmoitti odottavansa yhteistyötä uuden pääministerin kanssa.

## Pakistan haluaa laajentaa yhteistyötä

Myös Pakistanin presidentti Asif Ali Zardari ja pääministeri Shehbaz Sharif onnittelivat Burnhamia virkaan astumisesta. Zardari toivoi maiden pitkäaikaisen kumppanuuden vahvistuvan ja yhteistyön laajenevan yhteisten etujen mukaisilla aloilla.

Burnham on luvannut irtautua aiemmasta politiikasta ja rakentaa uuden talousmallin brittiläisten hyödyksi. Hänen mukaansa maa on kyllästynyt johtajien jatkuvaan vaihtumiseen. Lupaus nostaa talouspolitiikan keskeiseksi mittariksi sille, miten hänen hallituksensa onnistumista arvioidaan.

## Huomio kääntyy edessä oleviin haasteisiin

Diplomaattisten onnittelujen ohella kansainvälinen media painotti Burnhamia odottavan tehtävän mittakaavaa. Ranskalainen Public Sénat nosti esille hänen taustansa Pohjois-Englannin työväenluokassa sekä maanläheisen julkisuuskuvansa.

Kanava kuvaili Burnhamin rakentaneen itsestään tavallista kansalaista lähestyvän poliitikon kuvan. Hän on esiintynyt usein ilman solmiota ja toisinaan T-paidassa. Tällainen tyyli on tukenut vaikutelmaa arjen huolia tuntevasta alueellisesta poliitikosta, mutta pääministerinä hänen on nyt vastattava koko Britannian taloudellisiin ja poliittisiin odotuksiin.
summary_bullets: Kuningas Charles III nimitti Andy Burnhamin pääministeriksi Keir Starmerin erottua.
Euroopan johtajat korostivat Britannian kanssa tehtävän yhteistyön ja Ukraina-tuen jatkamista.
Kansainvälinen media kiinnitti onnittelujen lisäksi huomiota Burnhamia odottaviin suuriin haasteisiin.

Myös Pakistanin presidentti Asif Ali Zardari ja pääministeri Shehbaz Sharif onnittelivat Burnhamia virkaan astumisesta. Zardari toivoi maiden pitkäaikaisen kumppanuuden vahvistuvan ja yhteistyön laajenevan yhteisten etujen mukaisilla aloilla.

Burnham on luvannut irtautua aiemmasta politiikasta ja rakentaa uuden talousmallin brittiläisten hyödyksi. Hänen mukaansa maa on kyllästynyt johtajien jatkuvaan vaihtumiseen. Lupaus nostaa talouspolitiikan keskeiseksi mittariksi sille, miten hänen hallituksensa onnistumista arvioidaan.

## Huomio kääntyy edessä oleviin haasteisiin

Diplomaattisten onnittelujen ohella kansainvälinen media painotti Burnhamia odottavan tehtävän mittakaavaa. Ranskalainen Public Sénat nosti esille hänen taustansa Pohjois-Englannin työväenluokassa sekä maanläheisen julkisuuskuvansa.

Kanava kuvaili Burnhamin rakentaneen itsestään tavallista kansalaista lähestyvän poliitikon kuvan. Hän on esiintynyt usein ilman solmiota ja toisinaan T-paidassa. Tällainen tyyli on tukenut vaikutelmaa arjen huolia tuntevasta alueellisesta poliitikosta, mutta pääministerinä hänen on nyt vastattava koko Britannian taloudellisiin ja poliittisiin odotuksiin.

Beyond the diplomatic platitudes global media focuses on the ‘immense’ scale of the challenge he faces in the job World leaders have warmly congratulated Andy Burnham on his entry into 10 Downing Street as Britain’s seventh prime minister in a decade, but international media largely focused on the scale of the challenges awaiting him. Emmanuel Macron, France’s president, said he hoped for a deeper relationship “in the service of our peoples, and by giving new momentum to the partnership between the UK and the EU” rekindled by Burnham’s predecessor, Keir Starmer. The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, who spoke with Burnham on Monday evening including about continued support for Ukraine, said Germany and the UK were close partners and he looked forward to working together.

President hopes UK, under Burnham will contribute towards ending hostilities in ME and restoring Islamabad MoU President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday congratulated newly appointed United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham on assuming office and expressed their desire to strengthen cooperation with the incoming leader. Burnham became Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade, pledging to break with the politics of the past to deliver a new economic model to benefit a nation "fed up" with a revolving door of leaders. King Charles III appointed Burnham as prime minister after outgoing leader Keir Starmer formally tendered his resignation, Buckingham Palace said. According to a statement issued by the President's Office, Zardari hoped that under Burnham’s leadership, Pakistan and the UK would further strengthen their longstanding bilateral partnership and expand cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

The president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, said she looked forward to “strengthening the EU-UK partnership”. A “very good first discussion” had revealed a common commitment to “bringing the EU and UK closer and closer”, she later added. Beyond the diplomatic platitudes, however, media coverage focused on Burnham’s regional persona – and the huge task awaiting him. France’s Public Sénat said the new prime minister came from “the working class of the north of England”. He had managed to “build an image as an ‘everyman’, appearing without a tie, very often in a T-shirt”, the political TV channel said on its website, standing out as “a politician on the ground, close to everyday concerns”.
